sentences.text: Ritu Kindra vs Raghunandan K. on 16 February, 2023

Bench: Abhay S. Oka, Rajesh Bindal  IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA  CIVIL ORIGINAL JURISDICTION  TRANSFER PETITION (C) NO. 847 OF 2019  RITU KINDRA .....Petitioner(s  Vs.
 RAGHUNANDAN K. .....Respondent(s  O R D E R Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.
Perused the Settlement Agreement dated 29th November, 2022 executed before the learned Mediator of the Supreme Court Mediation Centre.
The Settlement Agreement has been signed by
the petitioner  wife, the respondent  husband and their respective advocates.

The learned counsel appearing for the parties state that all the terms and conditions incorporated in the Settlement Agreement have been complied with and that there is no impediment in the way of granting divorce by mutual consent.
The marriage between the parties was solemnized on 23rd November, 2015.
The parties have been residing separately from the year 2017.
After finding that the disputes and differences between them cannot be resolved, they have agreed to dissolve the marriage by mutual consent.

There are following proceedings pending between the parties :
Clauses 2 (ii to iv):
(ii) On 08.05.2019 : FIR No. 194/2019 was filed by Ms. Ritu u/s 498A, 323, 506, 313 of IPC, u/s 3, 4 of Dowry Act and u/s 67 of IT Act at Jhansi.
(iii) Domestic Violence, Case No.: 1151/2019 was filed by Ms. Ritu u/s 12, 17-20, 22 and 31 of Domestic Violence Act in P/S Mahila Thana, Nawabad, Jhansi.
(iv) Complaints for cyber bulling and harassment against the respondent were filed by Ms. Ritu and her friends on cybercrime.gov.in with acknowledgement Nos. 23107200045015.

In view of what is Ritu Kindra vs Raghunandan K. on 16 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/100013680/
1 stated in the Settlement Agreement, the proceedings/complainants mentioned above are hereby quashed.
We make it clear that no further steps shall be taken on the basis of the FIR and the complaint referred to in Clauses 2 (ii to iv) above.
Therefore, this is a fit case to exercise our jurisdiction under Article 142 of the Constitution of India.
Accordingly, the marriage solemnized between the parties on 23rd November, 2015 is hereby dissolved by a decree for divorce by mutual consent.
The terms and conditions incorporated in the Settlement Agreement shall form part of the decree.
The decree shall be drawn within maximum a period of six weeks from today.
All pending cases between the parties including the divorce petition  subject matter of this transfer petition stand disposed of in terms of the decree.
We record our appreciation for the reasonable stand taken by both the parties and their respective learned advocates as well as the role played by the Mediator.
...................J. (ABHAY S. OKA) ....................J (RAJESH BINDAL) New Delhi;
